requirements.requirement: Create the local account contractor on node1.
requirements.summary: The account was absent initially, then appeared in the local passwd database with UID/GID 1000, home /home/contractor, and shell /bin/bash; it remained intact after restart.
Direct shadow-database checks before and after restart report contractor's credential as password-set rather than locked.

requirements.requirement: Set contractor's maximum password age to 60 days.
requirements.summary: The local shadow entry directly reports max_days=60 both before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Set contractor's password-expiration warning period to 10 days.
requirements.summary: The local shadow entry directly reports warn_days=10 both before and after restart.

overall_summary: All public task outcomes are directly satisfied and persisted across restart. The mandatory node-restart protocol is complete: node1 was healthy before restart, acknowledged the restart, changed boot ID from be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad to 2f6afb7f-3305-4b28-a282-df6ae6935f5d, recovered to a running state with user sessions active, and retained the account and password-aging data. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the transition.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Account creation, password assignment, and aging-policy changes directly implemented the requested outcomes. The reboot was required by the provider-wide evidence protocol and was bounded and successful. All remaining commands were read-only verification or polling; the timed-out poll shows no additional mutation. Lifecycle differences are normal reboot effects: boot-scoped temporary directories and process identifiers changed, while sockets remained functionally equivalent, no failed services appeared, and package health remained sound.
